title: AI and Information Literacy Librarian
description:
AI and Information Literacy Librarian AI and Information Literacy Librarian University of Chicago Job Location: Date Created: 10/28/2026 Position Description The University of Chicago Library seeks a new team member to support our strategic priority to grow the scope and reach of the Library’s instructional programming for information literacy, digital skills, artificial intelligence (AI), and undergraduate research. The AI and Information Literacy Librarian will create, implement, and evaluate programs and services to help undergraduate students at the University of Chicago develop information literacy skills in the age of AI. The AI and Information Literacy Librarian reports to the Director of Teaching and Academic Engagement, and will be part of a unit dedicated to supporting the undergraduate experience and empowering students with the information literacy needed for academic success and life-long learning. We are looking for an individual who thrives in a team environment, is excited about experimentation and exploration, and envisions the library at the center of the undergraduate student experience. Responsibilities: Design and implement training for undergraduate students on the appropriate use of AI, including how to critically evaluate technology platforms, tools, and AI outputs, and understand the legal and ethical implications of its use (including academic honesty). Partner with the AI Librarian and other colleagues in the Center of Digital Scholarship to create instructional programs and materials promoting awareness and understanding of AI technologies and their implications for learning and research. Collaborate and consult with librarians, teaching faculty, and instructional designers to develop information and AI literacy programs for undergraduate courses and majors. Meet with undergraduates about using GenAI and research tools for assignments, capstone projects, research experiences, or future career opportunities. Provide teaching and reference support for the College’s new writing course, Inquiry, Conversation, Argument , focused on developing information literacy skills for first-year undergraduate students. Create online tutorials, research guides, and streaming videos to introduce students to the wide variety of tools and technologies available for their research and assignments. Serve on committees and workgroups focused on undergraduate teaching, instructional technology, and artificial intelligence. The Preservation Librarian provides strategic leadership and hands‑on direction for a comprehensive preservation program for the Reynolds-Finley Historical Library to ensure long‑term access to collections. This includes preventive care, such as environmental monitoring, integrated pest management, and stacks maintenance; conservation and repair of materials; digitization coordination; and digital preservation policy and practice. The Preservation Librarian assists with exhibition development as well as researchers and class visits to ensure proper handling of materials. Additionally, the Preservation Librarian will provide preservation support to the general collections of UAB Libraries as needed. Repository Details The Reynolds-Finley Historical Library is a collection of rare books, manuscripts, pamphlets, and journals pertaining to the history of medicine, science, and health care dating from the 1300s through the mid-1900s. The Reynolds-Finley Historical Library has eight medieval and Renaissance manuscripts and 32 incunabula, as well as letters written by Florence Nightingale, Louis Pasteur, and George Washington. In addition, discrete collections are held in the areas of Civil War medicine, Middle Eastern medicine, neurosurgery, otolaryngology, and African Americans in medicine. The Reynolds-Finley Historical Library is part of Historical Collections at UAB Libraries, which includes two additional collections: the Alabama Museum of the Health Sciences and UAB Archives. Together, the three units manage the Dennis G. Pappas Historical Collections Gallery, with nearly 3,000 square feet of exhibition space. UAB Libraries facilities include Lister Hill Library of the Health Sciences, where Historical Collections units are located, Mervyn H. Sterne Library, Lister Hill Library at University Hospital, Sparks Medical Library in Huntsville, and an off-site storage facility.
